messages:
Maya: Need a quick call on sequencing inference perf work for next sprint. Customers pushing on three asks: cut interactive latency, increase batch throughput, or reduce per-token cost. Can we sketch out a RICE-like prioritization and pick a lead by EOD?

Alex: Proposal: split into two concurrent tracks with separate owners — interactive (latency/p95) and bulk (throughput/cost). Interactive wins are faster to surface. Rough estimate: focused kernel selection + warm-cache optimization = ~2 sprints for measurable p95 drop.

Jia: Agreed on split. Quick RICE numbers to compare (very rough):
```
Latency-track: Reach=2 (interactive customers), Impact=5 (reduces timeouts), Confidence=0.6, Effort=6 => RICE=(2*5*0.6)/6=1.0
Throughput/cost-track: Reach=4, Impact=3, Confidence=0.7, Effort=9 => RICE=(4*3*0.7)/9=0.93
```
Narrow lead for latency. Note model mix matters: optimizations for 13B differ from 70B.

Vikram: From CS: finance & healthcare pilots have seen multiple interactive timeouts; they escalate quickly. High SLA risk on latency. Bulk embedding customers are high spend but less immediate risk. I recommend latency-first for next sprint. :point_up:

Sam: If we go latency-first, proposed acceptance criteria so PMs/devs can sign off:
- p95 end-to-end generation reduced >=25% on the interactive test suite
- No quality regression >1% on curated prompt set (logprobs/logit checks)
- Canary rollout with auto-fallback to previous model on error or p95 spike
- Observability: token-level spend + cold/warm cache p50/p95 reported
If we meet these, we expand to multi-region.

Ellie: Add SRE gating: require synthetic canary traffic and a rollback window. Define thresholds: if canary p95 > baseline*1.15 or error rate >0.5% revert. Also include KV-cache hit-rate metric — if hit rate falls >10% from baseline, halt rollout.

Alex: Dev estimates for latency-track (rough): runtime selector refactor 5d, prefix/KV cache tuning 4d, metrics/canary plumbing 3d, perf validation & QA 3d. Total ~15 dev-days ~2 engineers => 2 sprints.

Jia: QA note: quantization or kernel swaps can change sampling behavior. Add an eval harness step: run 200 golden prompts, compare BLEU/QA metrics and top-k logits distribution. Block on >1% quality delta.

Maya: Sounds like a plan. Can someone draft a short PRD with two options: A) Latency-first (owner, timeline, acceptance criteria) and B) Cost-first (owner, timeline, acceptance criteria). We'll meet 15m tomorrow 11:00 PT to decide. Please include the metrics & rollback thresholds.

Alex: I will draft the PRD and a one-page sequencing plan by 6pm today. Will include a minimal rollout plan and owners.

Vikram: I'll attach 2 customer logs and the affected flow examples to the PRD so the severity is visible.

Sam: Scheduling 11:00 PT slot. Agenda: choose sequence, name owners, finalize canary thresholds.

Ellie: I'll add the runbook steps and rollback play to the PRD (how to flip fallback, which metrics to watch, paging list).

deploy-bot: heads-up — maintenance on perf-cluster scheduled Tue 03:00-06:00 UTC; avoid running long perf baselines then.

Maya: Noted, thanks. Final note: if anyone has data to push the RICE confidence higher, drop it in the PRD. Otherwise we'll go latency-first unless someone objects in tomorrow's call. :thumbsup:
